root_idea.summary: The root is oriented toward entering or penetrating into a house, lair, or other enclosed place, with a distinct Quranic causative branch describing the imposition of ruin.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence connects entry into a place with stealthy entry into a hunting lair, while the Quranic Form II branch specifically develops the meaning of bringing destruction or perdition upon something.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form.
Displayed separately as the Quran-attested Form II verbal noun.

senses.definition: To destroy utterly; to bring ruin or perdition upon someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative verb. In the Quranic construction with عَلَى, the object may be understood from context, as in دَمَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ.

senses.definition: The act or result of bringing destruction, ruin, or perdition upon something.
senses.usage_conditions: The verbal noun of دَمَّرَ; it can denote the destructive action or its resulting devastation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perish, or to perish utterly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a people or a thing. The related infinitive دُمُورٌ is also cited for a transitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To intrude upon people or enter a dwelling without permission, especially in an offensive manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction with عَلَى, as in دَمَرَ عَلَيْهِمْ; the entry may be physical or socially intrusive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a sportsman, to fumigate a hunting lair with fur or soft animal hair so that game will not detect his scent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized hunting use distinct from the Quranic meaning of causing destruction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass the night sleepless, or to endure and brave the difficulty of the night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form III expression marked as figurative or extended usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ewe or she-goat having little milk.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate descriptive use of the same adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or group given to intruding upon others or entering their quarters without permission.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a woman and also to others, including a company of people; the gendered example does not restrict the meaning.
The nouns are used for a state of perdition, as in the expression حَلَّ بِهِمُ الدَّمَارُ, 'perdition befell them.'

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man in a state of perdition, with no good in him; an erring and perishing man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of jerboa that is small and short, described as of vile make, with broken nails and tough flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is also identified as the مَاعِز kind of jerboa; the descriptions record specialized zoological distinctions.
An extended expression, explicitly marked as figurative or assumed figurative.
In مَا فِي الدَّارِ تَدْمُرِيٌّ, the expression means that there is no one in the house.
The type is distinguished from dogs called سَلُوقِيَّةٌ and كُرْدِيَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sportsman who fumigates his hunting lair with camel fur or other soft hair to conceal his scent; by extension, a skilled sportsman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized hunting designation, associated with rushing upon game unseen.
